missions.statement: Develop LaneNote Core as a CDN-loadable browser-local plugin that renders the source note into a timeline-by-assignee Lens without server dependency.

stakeholders.name: PM note author
stakeholders.role: Primary user who writes informal notes and needs assignment/date visibility without cleanup work.

stakeholders.name: Noblit or host-page integrator
stakeholders.role: Consumer that embeds the LaneNote Core runtime via a script tag or equivalent CDN path.

contexts.title: Browser-local CDN plugin
contexts.description: The runtime is loaded as a plain browser script, exposes window.LaneNoteCore, and operates without npm installation or a backend service.

contexts.title: AOF-governed implementation flow
contexts.description: Development evidence must include at least one relevant AOF runtime command and QIF validation evidence.

risks.statement: The plugin cannot be consumed from a CDN-style script tag or does not expose a stable global API.
risks.lossBoundary: Host pages must not require a build step or server dependency to mount the MVP renderer.

risks.statement: Lens interactions, substring inference, noisy rendering, or repeated rendering mutate source meaning, hide the user's intended view, or lose the distinction between scheduled and due dates.
risks.lossBoundary: Checkbox updates must round-trip through the source line; title text must not be damaged by assignee detection; scheduled and due dates must coexist; relative dates must not drift after the line receives its writing timestamp; routine provenance must not crowd the card surface when it does not change user action.

risks.statement: Activity such as writing code, running tests, or passing a validator is overstated as semantic product quality.
risks.lossBoundary: The project must not claim release-ready semantic quality from structural/runtime checks alone.

qualityIntents.statement: LaneNote Core must be embeddable as a CDN-style browser plugin with a stable global API for parsing, mounting, rendering, source access, and teardown.
qualityIntents.purpose: Protect host-page integration from build-tool and server coupling.
acceptanceCriteria: dist/lanenote-core.js exposes LaneNoteCore.version, create, parse, renderMatrix, getDefaultProfile, getDefaultTemplates, exportProjectedMarkdown, exportPortableJSON, and replaceCheckboxAtLine.
examples/browser-local.html consumes the runtime through a script tag and exposes project-management templates linked to each built-in Lens.

qualityIntents.statement: The browser-local Lens must preserve the source note as truth and sync checkbox state by editing the corresponding Markdown checkbox line.
qualityIntents.purpose: Protect user trust and prevent hidden derived-state divergence.
acceptanceCriteria: Rule parser preserves separate scheduledAt, dueAt, eventAt, and recordedAt values while retaining a compatibility projection date.
Unknown structural assignee headings become lanes, aliases resolve through the textarea DSL or host fallback profile, and arbitrary title substrings do not become assignees.
Only checkbox items receive Open or Done task state; non-checkbox items remain notes or action/event candidates.
Browser block metadata gives each line a stable ID and writing timestamp used to freeze relative-date interpretation.
Lens axis orientation, grouping, and folding alter only the derived view without mutating the source note.
Built-in and host-defined templates are filtered by active Lens; applying one explicitly replaces source text and switches to its declared Lens.
The textarea source contains the complete LaneNote DSL for Lens, role, group, alias, filter, and note-body definitions; host profile data is only a fallback.
Front matter lens and filters set initial view state without mutating source text and renderMatrix respects them when explicit runtime options are not provided.
Card chips are reserved for actionable or disambiguating information rather than every derived field.
Projected Markdown export follows current filters, axis orientation, grouping/folding visibility, and source-line evidence without rewriting the source note.
replaceCheckboxAtLine updates both leading and inline Markdown checkbox markers.

qualityIntents.statement: Implementation claims must remain tied to AOF runtime evidence and QIF loss boundaries rather than activity counts.
qualityIntents.purpose: Protect review quality by separating structural/runtime evidence from semantic product approval.
acceptanceCriteria: At least one AOF runtime command is executed and retained as evidence.
QIF package passes the local QIF validator while explicitly limiting verifier claims.

evidenceItems.finding: Node VM execution of dist/lanenote-core.js verifies the v0.2 global API, default profile fallback exposure, full textarea DSL for Lens/role/group/filter definitions, compact context syntax, separate scheduled and due dates, structural unknown-role discovery, exact-prefix alias recognition, OpenAI substring preservation, Task versus candidate state, per-line relative-date bases, invalid-date rejection, source-local multi-axis Lens profiles, reduced routine provenance chips, view-linked templates, group rendering, human Markdown export, portable JSON, and checkbox source-line replacement.
AOF runtime command initialized LaneNote as a managed-project with runtime-on mode and produced .aof bootstrap, orientation, organization, registry, policy, resource, capability, and goal artifacts.
The requirements draft identifies source-note truth, timeline-by-assignee Lens, local-first operation, and checkbox bidirectional sync as MVP boundaries.

governanceEvents.statement: Human/operator review is still required before claiming Noblit integration readiness or public release readiness.

criteria.statement: Browser-local demo exists and loads the runtime through a script tag.
Implemented syntax is documented as an auditable artifact.
Runtime test exists for parser, API exposure, and checkbox source-line sync.
AOF runtime bootstrap exists for governed execution evidence.
